correctness.rationale: The 2-uniform order-preserving mapping of parent suffixes to odd-position next-level suffixes proves the sentinel recursion; replacing parent terminal zero by a cyclic seam comparison symbol one still preserves order because all other comparison symbols are at least two, proving the cyclic recursion. Explicit induction yields every output symbol; small levels \(n=1,2\) are separately accounted for; for \(n\ge3\) every displayed block has positive length and changes symbol. Independent direct rotation and suffix-doubling computations match through \(n=16\); finite verification is not used as infinite proof.

evidence: Ferenczi–Zamboni (2023), Section 2 Definition 1 and Theorem 1, studies clustering, which demands contiguous symbols and at most one block per letter.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The studied Zimin cyclic outputs have \(2n-1>n\) runs for all \(n\ge3\); thus they do not satisfy the clustering hypothesis and the clustering classification cannot imply the claimed full output. Asymptotic fixed-alphabet growth statements do not entail all block exponents.

originality.rationale: The cyclic and terminal-symbol transforms are computed in full for every Zimin level. Detailed searches of indexed literature and mathematical records, plus inspection of the foundational BWT report, primary Zimin literature, fixed-alphabet morphic BWT papers, and episturmian clustering papers, found no identical or logically stronger statement that yields these descending-block formulas. The strongest apparent episturmian clustering characterization is inapplicable: clustering entails ≤n runs for an n-letter alphabet, whereas these Zimin outputs have \(2n-1\) runs for \(n\ge3\). An unindexed equivalence or unexamined broader source remains a residual risk; absence from databases is not treated as proof of uniqueness.
residual_risks: Indexing misses preprints or formulations without Zimin in title/keywords; no absolute novelty proof is asserted.
All claims are bounded to the specified ordered alphabet and exact cyclic/sentinel conventions; different conventions produce different output.

value.rationale: This gives two full closed-form BWT strings for every level of a canonical recursively palindromic pattern rather than a run-growth bound alone. It explains by exact suffix ordering why all \(2^n-1\) alternating runs in the input become only \(2n-1\) linear runs in the cyclic transform, an explicit and nontrivial structural phenomenon relevant to run-length text indexes, with a growing alphabet caveat.
